candidates.angle: Kṛṣṇa checks if Arjuna listened with a one-pointed mind
candidates.evidence: त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा (by you with one-pointed mind)

candidates.angle: Kṛṣṇa asks if the delusion born of ignorance has been destroyed
candidates.evidence: अज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टः (delusion born of ignorance destroyed)

candidates.angle: Kṛṣṇa addresses Arjuna by two names, Partha and Dhananjaya

angle_hi: एकाग्रेण चेतसा: एक बिंदु में इकट्ठी चेतना

en.intro: Krishna has finished his long teaching and turns to Arjuna, checking whether the words have landed. The war still waits, but the real test is whether Arjuna's ignorance and confusion have been broken.
en.notice: Krishna asks two questions, one about listening and one about being free. The word krsna uses for listening, srutam, is just the past tense of hearing, and he asks if Arjuna heard this with ekagrena cetasa, a mind gathered into a single point.
en.next: Arjuna answers that his delusion is gone and he will do as Krsna says.
en.meaning: O Partha, have you heard this with one-pointed mind? O Dhananjaya, has the delusion born of ignorance been destroyed in you?

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अपना लंबा उपदेश समाप्त कर लिया है और अब अर्जुन की ओर मुड़कर यह देख रहे हैं कि उनका ज्ञान उन तक पहुँचा या नहीं। युद्ध अभी भी बाकी है, लेकिन असली परीक्षा यह है कि क्या अर्जुन का अज्ञान और भ्रम टूट गया है।
hi.meaning: हे पृथानन्दन, क्या तुमने एकाग्रचित्त से इसको सुना और हे धनञ्जय, क्या तुम्हारा अज्ञान से उत्पन्न मोह नष्ट हुआ?
hi.notice: कृष्ण दो सवाल पूछते हैं, एक सुनने का और एक मुक्त होने का। सुनने के लिए वे जिस शब्द का उपयोग करते हैं, श्रुतम्, वह केवल सुनने के भूतकाल का रूप है, और वे पूछते हैं कि क्या तुमने इसे एकाग्रेण चेतसा, यानी एक बिंदु में इकट्ठी हुई चेतना से सुना।
hi.next: अर्जुन जवाब देते हैं कि उनका मोह नष्ट हो गया है और वे कृष्ण के कहे अनुसार करेंगे।

en.intro: Krishna has finished his long teaching and turns to Arjuna, checking whether the words have landed. The war still waits, but the real test is whether Arjuna's ignorance and confusion have been broken.
en.body: O Partha, have you heard this with one-pointed mind? O Dhananjaya, has the delusion born of ignorance been destroyed in you? Krishna asks two questions, one about listening and one about being free. The word krsna uses for listening, srutam, is just the past tense of hearing, and he asks if Arjuna heard this with ekagrena cetasa, a mind gathered into a single point. Arjuna answers that his delusion is gone and he will do as Krsna says.
